phase0a_antiControls.detail: 10/10 PASS — 9 adversarial scenarios each produced HALT_UNSAFE_FIXTURE with zero destructive signals; healthy control delivered exactly 1 signal. Machine-checks the P1 non-delivery authorization-denial contract.

phase0a_classifierContract.detail: 7/7 PASS — only ESRCH yields GONE; EPERM yields UNVERIFIABLE whether or not the process table is readable.

phase0_preflight.detail: dogfood main=77086, extension-host=77158, extension-host uid == operator uid.

phase1_installedArtifactIdentity.detail: The installed bundle SHA-256 is 7aba56e769d322adb420f79f5c161e5bd4abb260761ff25a4ba73ace3e1fd0f9, NOT the required e35de822bec46b697fad7e651206d73124796b2179c2e6a25a083adced6a8a66. The installed extension directory is s1onique.clinemm-4.1.16-5a1c485cb-1f456b971, a build that PREDATES the permanent repair commit d038b1e00. It still contains the retired CLINEMM_DIAG_SAME_SANDBOX_SIGNAL gate (2 occurrences), the retired armSeatbeltSignalRuleAuthorization export (1), and the pre-repair signalTarget selector that emits '(allow signal (target self))'.
phase1_installedArtifactIdentity.installAttempt: operator-qualification.sh install FAILED — 'codium --install-extension' could not mkdir in the dogfood extensions dir (EPERM) nor in the dogfood logs dir (EPERM).
phase1_installedArtifactIdentity.substrateCause: The agent substrate is itself confined by a Seatbelt profile whose write roots do not include /Volumes/UserData/Users/chistyakov/.vscodium-clinemm. mkdir, touch and cp into that tree all fail with EPERM. This reproduces the ceiling already recorded in raw/substrate-limitation.txt section 4 and is an environment limit, not a code defect.
phase1_installedArtifactIdentity.vsixVerifiedCorrect: dist/clinemm-signal-repair01.vsix (sha256 f638ff5ed0bb631c0f347b8e2ee9a4d5a8af9fb651769fa345665d037cce3d81) extracts to extension/dist/extension.js with sha256 e35de822...a8a66, carries '(allow signal (target same-sandbox))' and ZERO traces of the retired diagnostic markers.

phase1_loadedBundleIdentity.detail: The bundle actually LOADED by the dogfood extension host was captured from the LIVE Seatbelt profile it generated. The live profile contains '(allow signal (target self))' — the PRE-REPAIR rule — while the permanent repair requires '(allow signal (target same-sandbox))'. Reproduced twice (prepareCallId 447 and 452 in observer run signal-exact-1793898271).
phase1_loadedBundleIdentity.method: Captured the ephemeral profile file from the observer's own profilePath while a Background Exec command was in flight; the profile is deleted after use, so it was read live.
phase1_loadedBundleIdentity.conclusion: A matching on-disk VSIX is NOT the loaded artifact. The loaded artifact is the pre-repair build.

phase1_observerEnabled.detail: The dogfood extension host DOES carry CLINEMM_CAPTURE_SANDBOX=1 and CLINEMM_RUNTIME_PROFILE=dogfood, and the observer is live (1281+ correlated events). But its run id is 'signal-exact-1793898271', not the runbook's 'repair01-qualification', so operator-qualification.sh identity would abort.

phase2_productionGreenThroughBackgroundE.detail: Blocked upstream by the installed-artifact-identity failure. The live seam currently runs the PRE-REPAIR profile, so a production GREEN would measure the pre-repair build, not the permanent repair.

phase3_observerCorrelation.detail: The observer correlation MECHANISM is proven working end-to-end: prepareCallId, profilePath, profile sha256, onPrepareInput.commandExecutable (/bin/zsh), onInvocationPrepared.executable (/usr/bin/sandbox-exec) and the exact argv are all recorded and correlate with the live profile. The specific Phase-2 correlation for the permanent repair cannot be produced because that profile was never generated.

phase4_pgidCancellation.detail: The fixture ran through the real Background Exec seam and refused safely: halt=HALT_UNSAFE_FIXTURE, haltReason='identity-incomplete:argv,startIdentity,uid,pgid', groupOwnershipHeld=false, destructiveSignalsIssued=[]. The cause is that inside the pre-repair sandbox the process-table observation of the child returns EPERM and kill(child,0) returns EPERM, so the identity cannot be established and no group-directed signal is attempted. Zero destructive signals were issued.
phase4_pgidCancellation.interpretation: This is a SAFE refusal under the pre-repair profile. It is not evidence that the permanent repair fails; the permanent repair was never loaded.

phase5_foreignProcessDenial.detail: The fixture ran through the real Background Exec seam and refused safely: halt=HALT_UNSAFE_FIXTURE, haltReason='identity-incomplete:argv,startIdentity,uid,pgid', authorizationCheck={state:'alive',errnoCode:'EPERM',deliversSignal:false}, signalAttempt={ok:false,skipped:true}, destructiveSignalsIssued=[], foreignAliveBefore=true. The foreign target received NO signal.
phase5_foreignProcessDenial.p1ContractNote: The result took the identity-incomplete branch (process-table observation failed), so authorizationDenial is null. The P1 two-shape contract covers the target-unsignalable:EPERM branch, which the eperm-target anti-control exercises and machine-checks.
phase5_foreignProcessDenial.cleanup: PASS. foreign-stop first reported UNVERIFIABLE while the target was still inside its 12s lifetime — correct fail-closed behaviour, EPERM is never accepted as cleanup. After the target self-exited, foreign-stop reported 'PASS: pid=4728 is gone' (verified by ESRCH). Orphan check: NO ORPHANS.

phase6_vitestWorkerTeardown.detail: The focused suite passed 11/11 with exit code 0, but the output contains 'Failed to terminate forks worker ... Error: kill EPERM' once. The cause is again the pre-repair '(allow signal (target self))' rule denying the teardown SIGTERM.
phase6_vitestWorkerTeardown.exactWorkerIdentityVerification: The worker was observed live during the run: PID 8859, start identity 'Thu Nov  5 23:42:02 2026', argv '<node> .../vitest/dist/workers/forks.js'. After the run that exact PID was verified GONE by PID + argv + start identity. ORPHANS_LEFT_BY_THIS_RUN=0.
phase6_vitestWorkerTeardown.runbookGate: The runbook gate requires the output NOT to contain 'Failed to terminate forks worker'. That message IS present, so the gate as written is NOT satisfied — but the message is attributable to the pre-repair bundle, not to the permanent repair. This gate must be re-measured after the permanent bundle is installed.
phase6_vitestWorkerTeardown.hostContext: 27 orphaned forks workers already existed on the host, every one of them started before this qualification run (latest 20:33; this run was 23:41-23:42). They are pre-existing substrate state, not produced by this qualification.

blockingDefect.statement: The dogfood extension host is running s1onique.clinemm-4.1.16-5a1c485cb-1f456b971, a build that predates the permanent repair. Its live Seatbelt profile carries '(allow signal (target self))'. The correct permanent artifact exists on disk (dist/clinemm-signal-repair01.vsix, bundle sha256 e35de822...a8a66) but cannot be installed from this substrate because the agent sandbox's write roots exclude the dogfood extensions directory.
blockingDefect.operatorActionRequired: From an ordinary (unsandboxed) Terminal on this host: run 'bash .factory/evidence/ACT-CLINEMM-BACKGROUND-EXEC-SAME-SANDBOX-SIGNAL-REPAIR01/operator-qualification.sh install', then reload ONLY the dogfood VSCodium window, then re-run the five live phases in the runbook order.
